name: subagent-isolation
context: Multi-agent systems where parallel subagents operate in independent workspaces to prevent file-level conflicts and enable safe concurrent execution. Each subagent works in its own isolated context — writes do not collide, and the orchestrator synthesizes results from distilled summaries rather than retaining full subagent context.
benefits: Eliminates file-level write conflicts in concurrent agent execution
Prevents context pollution between independent subagent reasoning traces
Enables true parallelism without coordination locks
Orchestrator can selectively recall full evidence from any subagent run on demand
tradeoffs: Subagents cannot coordinate mid-flight on tightly coupled findings
Synthesis quality depends on the quality of subagent summary distillation
Isolation boundaries require careful workspace provisioning
Debugging requires querying across isolated run contexts
use_cases: Incident investigation: three agents dig logs, attempt reproduction, and check history concurrently
Code migration: agents modifying different files of the same codebase simultaneously
Research synthesis: agents exploring different source categories in parallel
Batch document processing: agents handling disjoint document sets concurrently
avoid_when: Subtasks must react to each other's findings in real time
All work must share a single context window
Workspace provisioning overhead exceeds the parallelism gain
anti_patterns: Using isolation when tasks share mutable state — leads to silent inconsistencies
Returning only distilled summaries with no way to access full subagent evidence
Failing to link subagent runs back to the orchestrator for traceability
Unbounded parallel spawns without concurrency caps causing cost spikes
Returning free-text instead of schema artifacts that cannot be parsed
Subagent inherits parent history causing context bloat
design_principles: Each subagent workspace must be independently durable — no shared filesystem
Subagent findings must be written as structured observations before returning
The orchestrator must be able to query across all linked subagent runs on demand
Each subagent must enforce independent runtime budgets: max_tokens_in, max_tokens_out, max_steps, wall_clock_timeout
Cap parallel subagent spawns with a concurrency limit; queue excess work with backpressure
best_practices: Use run IDs to link each subagent execution back to the orchestrator session
Write observations as structured facts (not just a text summary) for queryable recall
Test that cross-run queries correctly combine evidence from all subagents
Define a typed result envelope (Pydantic model or JSON Schema) for subagent returns with required fields: verdict, findings[], citations[], uncertainty_level, status_code
Return structured failure artifacts on error with fields: error_code, retryable (boolean), user_message
Propagate trace_id from parent; assign unique run_id per child with span events: child_spawned, child_completed, child_failed
Use idempotent spawn keys (parent_run_id + subtask_id) so resume does not duplicate expensive operations
references: Huang et al., AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation, 2023 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155
